title: Gifts of travel filed, but not on the official’s Form 700
question: When an elected officer files a gift-of-travel form for a trip someone else paid for, does the same trip appear on that officer’s annual statement of economic interests (Form 700)?
finding: Of 143 gift-of-travel filings from 2015 to 2026 (amendments and duplicates set aside), 116 of the 124 that can be checked appear as a gift or travel payment on the officer’s Form 700 (93.5%). 8 trips worth $15,718.38, filed by 7 officers, are missing from a Form 700 that is on file for the period. Another 10 trips ($59,340.49) have no statement on file for the period at all, all of them Mayor Edwin Lee’s 2017 trips; 7 trips of 2026 are not yet due. 2 filings ($1,113.00) were made on the elected officers’ form by a Public Health staff member, who is not named, and are not on that person’s statements either.
how: Gifts of Travel filings (current set snqf-y894 and the legacy set uqhk-vesf, April 2015 to March 2018), one per trip. Each officer is matched to Form 700 statements by first name and surname; a trip counts as listed when a Schedule D gift or Schedule E travel entry of the same officer starts within 14 days of the trip. The cover pages give the statement that covers each trip date and its count of Schedule D and E entries.
limits: The gift-of-travel form is also filed when the officer reimburses the cost, and a trip paid by a government body or a school may not belong on Schedule E; either would leave nothing to list. An amended Form 700 that is not in the open data, or an entry under another name or a date more than 14 days off, would also show here as missing. The Board’s communications for December 2017 (File 180018) record condolences on the passing of Mayor Lee; no statement covers his 2017 trips. The open data does not show who paid the legacy trips unless the note names the payer. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
